items.title: A compact object of the derived category of a dg algebra is bounded
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dga.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-compact-implies-bounded at source lines 6562-6569: for a dg algebra (A,d) and a compact object E of D(A,d) there are integers a <= b such that Hom(E,M) vanishes whenever M has no cohomology in degrees a..b. The proof at source lines 6571-6582 first observes that the objects admitting such a bound form a saturated strictly full triangulated subcategory, then applies the author's compactness proposition to reduce to modules with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are finite sums of shifts of A, and finally to P = A, where the bound is a = b = 0 because Hom(A,M) = H^0(M). It is short; the substance is recognising that the boundedness condition is triangulated-subcategory closed and that the compactness proposition is exactly the tool for the reduction.
